title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: additive Cheon at the success floor (K=0.4952), a measured side-output kernel, synchronous wave transport, a re-counted per-record transport listing, a charged planner state with 32-bit relative-offset pointers, and a corrected pair midpoint load

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.3900 (required 0.39) over the uniform challenge and fresh algorithm coins. It is Cheon's attack in the subgroup H of 2^20-th powers (d = 2^20 divides r-1, 6d divides r-1, A_d is read; only A_1 and A_d are used). Baby and giant scalars are products a*b in H with a a prime of (2^76, 2^76 + 2^70] taken in increasing order and b a class integer <= 2^76 with chi(b) = -chi(a). Each class list is planned offline into three-term progressions (x-g, x, x+g) with g <= 2^44 = 16 d^2 (depth cap 2^14, tree cap 2^20, restart segments of 2^24 entries, handed to lanes greedily in plan order so every lane finishes within one segment of the others); the planner keeps 32-byte per-element records (parent, partner, depth, height, pair-slot, tree size, child-list head/next), charged in the planning-node memory row, whose four pointer fields are signed 32-bit offsets from the element's own absolute class-list index (null sentinel -2^31; every target lies in the 2^26-member planner window so |offset| < 2^27 < 2^31, and the executable plan() stores and decodes these fields with a rel32() bound assert), and the repeated set_depth/height traversals over the stored child lists are charged by an explicit worst-case ledger row (4 l max_tree visits at 16 instructions plus l DEPTH height steps at 8 per class = 64 max_tree + 8 DEPTH per element), whose 16 per visit include the 3-instruction ldr/sxtw/add pointer decode and whose 64 per emitted element include the pointer encodes, not by the 8/point allowance, and the walk computes [a(x+g)]Q = P+T as the reference batched incomplete affine addition (2000 instructions) and [a(x-g)]Q = P-T, with its orbit key, by one AArch64 function sharing the lane inverse, measured at 1127 instructions per lane in the organizers' Callgrind pipeline (blst routines verbatim, self-checked against blst's exported API and genuine curve points; measure/), and the key extraction for P+T and the root uses the same measured 17-instruction sequence (6-limb p - Y, 6-limb compare, 3 csel, 3-word store); the planned pair fraction is at least f = 0.98 (heuristic H4). Generating nodes run 2^18 lanes over one base and one gap table with one batched inversion per round. Records are 40 bytes (192-bit truncated U-orbit key, 128-bit chain id), matched in direct-mapped head arrays chained through pools at 2^60 owner nodes. Transport is a synchronous wave protocol over a cluster whose only inter-node mechanism is a store into a write-mapped per-link receive buffer plus a doorbell interrupt: two charged hops (generating node -> relay -> owner), every word stored by the sender and loaded by the receiver at every hop, preallocated per-link buffers and count words at fixed caps for both parities of a double buffering, one global barrier per wave through an explicit fan-in-2^10 tree with every wake, sweep and release charged, no credits, no retries, no polling; a cap overflow is a counted run failure (H3 tails); candidates and replies travel the same links in two further rounds; candidates are resolved by one bounded re-walk of each record's plan segment and at most 96 scalar tests, all charged at the 2^44 cap; an explicit allowance of 8 instructions per point is a ledger row. Total work W(2^20) is at most 2^116.365531 target-group-operation equivalents (exact score 116365531/1000000), including both walks and their gap tables, restarts, padding, matching and comparisons, transport words and barriers, plan construction and distribution, the character sieves and base search, candidate handling, the d-th root, the mu_d search and input access. Preprocessing (challenge-independent work) is at most 2^115.3650 units and is included. Peak memory is at most 2^121.5854 bytes, every per-node total below 2^63 bytes; there is no nonuniform advice. Heuristics, all disclosed in proof.md with toy evidence at its stated scope: H1 (coverage |R|/m >= 1 - e^{-K} - 0.0005 at the realized K >= 0.4952, supported by an exact census of the construction on toy primes up to m = 2^32 in which every modular and rational coincidence is measured, never excluded by size), H2 (character equidistribution and the class/base bounds, affecting only charged terms and buffer bounds, with a stop-and-fail rule), H3 (keys as uniform strings, with every cap and tail bounded and overflow counted as failure), H4 (pair fraction >= 0.98; the production window/tree-cap ratio 2*GMAX/d^2 = 32 is exercised by matched cap-active planner controls at d = 8,16,32,64,128 with max_tree = d on the same real class lists as the uncapped controls, where the cap binds with 2135-4635 size rejections; the measured cap excess decays as B/d with B = 1.31-1.65, so at production d = 2^20 it is at most 2.2/2^20 = 2.1e-6, while the uncapped fraction rises with d to 0.9879 at d = 128, leaving a 7.8e-3 margin above the claimed 0.98), H5 (Poisson-like candidate multiplicity, with the total-candidate tails at the exact unconditional mean and the per-run true-hit multiplicity Markov-bounded at its conditional mean 1.28). This is an analytic bound with a measured kernel and itemised instruction counts, not a full-size execution. The coverage heuristic H1 applies at K=0.4952 and is not a consequence of acceptance of the predecessor at K=0.5; the predecessor census at K=0.5 provides indirect support only. The sample size N is the least integer with 6*N^2 >= 0.4952*m.

experiments.purpose: One run with five parts. (1) ledger: recomputes every cost term of proof.md section 6 from exact integers, the exact score with its boundary assert, the preprocessing and memory inequalities (every per-node total below 2^63 bytes), the success inequality with every failure term, and the production algebra identities; arithmetic only. (2) planner: the offline pairing planner of proof.md section 3 (depth and tree-size caps) on real chi-class lists of toy primes at the production degree parameter GMAX = 16 d^2; reports pair fraction, cycle and size rejections, dependency depth and tree size against the caps (evidence for H4). (3) ec: the whole algorithm on a toy j = 0 curve with 2 not in H: planned paired walk with the shared-inversion pair formula, ordered disjoint bases, truncated-key bucket matching with false matches counted, bounded re-walk, six-z resolution, d-th root and mu_d scan; success against prediction, every recovered scalar verified, every sampled collision event checked against the exact coverage of the independently reconstructed emitted sets. (4) proto: the section-4 synchronous wave transport at toy scale: per-link receive buffers with caps and double buffering, relays, owners, a fan-in barrier tree with worst-case wakes and sweeps, candidate and reply rounds; asserts exact delivery, the buffer discipline (read exactly in the wave after the write), candidate resolution, cap overflow as a run failure, and that the simulated instruction total (the listing applied to counted events) equals the ledger's closed form; three key patterns. (5) census: the exact coverage |R|/m of the construction on a toy prime at the production scaling rule, with the exact multiplicity diagnostic (evidence for H1 and H5). Toy parts are evidence at toy/simulation scope only; the kernel price is measured separately (measure/).
